transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?
I keep getting hit out of nowhere with the image of my cousin on the pavement. I can hear the shouting and see the lights again, even when I’m just standing in the church office trying to act normal.
How long ago did the accident involving your cousin happen?
It was two years and three months ago, when my cousin was killed.
Since the accident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or situations that remind you of what happened to your cousin?
Yeah. I take the long way around town so I don’t have to go past the community center or the court. And if someone starts talking about that night, I usually shut it down or find a reason to leave.

latest_inference.note: Symptoms have persisted for over two years with intrusive flashbacks, sensory re-experiencing (sounds/lights), and deliberate avoidance of reminders (places, conversations). This chronic, full symptom cluster of re-experiencing plus avoidance is inconsistent with adjustment disorder (F43.20), which typically resolves within 6 months and lacks true flashbacks. This narrows the diagnosis to PTSD.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a clearly identifiable traumatic event (witnessing/learning of cousin's violent death) over two years ago, followed by persistent, vivid intrusive re-experiencing (visual flashbacks, auditory recollections of shouting/lights) occurring involuntarily in unrelated settings (work). This is accompanied by deliberate avoidance of trauma-associated cues (specific locations, conversations about the event). The chronicity (>1 month, in fact >2 years), the specificity of intrusive re-experiencing tied to a discrete traumatic index event, and active avoidance behavior are core diagnostic features of PTSD (F43.1) rather than an adjustment disorder or generalized anxiety, which lack the intrusive re-experiencing phenomenon and direct trauma linkage.

confirmed_symptoms: Involuntary vivid flashbacks of cousin on the pavement
Visual intrusions (seeing lights) recurring in unrelated contexts (at work)
Avoids specific locations associated with the trauma (community center, court)
Avoids or shuts down conversations referencing the traumatic night
Leaves situations when trauma-related topics arise

additional_requirements: Clear identifiable traumatic event (cousin's violent death) established
